newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. sailor arrested in Japan in sex assault case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sailor arrested in Japan in sex assault case.

text.p: An American sailor is under arrest at the headquarters base of the U.S. Navy in Japan on suspicion of beating and sexually assaulting his Japanese girlfriend in his quarters, police said on Thursday.
A police spokesman said the incident at Yokosuka Naval Base on the outskirts of Tokyo did not appear to involve rape and happened during an argument between the pair.

No formal charges had yet been filed in Wednesday's incident, which could cause new tensions in U.S.-Japan relations after the widely publicised 1995 gang rape of a Japanese schoolgirl on Okinawa by three U.S. servicemen.
The incident also came as U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen prepared to visit Japan and South Korea next week.

"He is under arrest and we will know more details as the investigation unfolds," Cohen told reporters in Washington in response to questions during a Pentagon photo opportunity with Jordan's King Hussein.
Japanese police said the 21-year-old woman had told them the couple had dated for about eight months and her injuries happened during a quarrel over a "small thing".
Yokosuka deputy police chief Satoshi Nakajima told Reuters the woman said her 27-year-old boyfriend grabbed her during the argument and then dropped her on a bed.
She bounced off the bed and fell on the floor, breaking her collarbone, the police quoted her as saying.
"Apparently, this is not a case of rape," Nakajima told Reuters.

A U.S. Navy spokesman at Yokosuka said the petty officer third class was being questioned by the Navy's Criminal Investigative Service after security forces responded to a disturbance at the bachelor's enlisted quarters on the base.

"Upon arrival (at the quarters), they found a 21-year-old Japanese woman who had been beaten and allegedly sexually assaulted by an E-4 (third class petty officer) assigned to Yokosuka Naval Computer and Telecommunications Station," the spokesman said.
"She was taken to the U.S. Naval Hospital at Yokosuka where she was treated for a broken clavicle, abrasions and contusions," he added.
"The E-4 was taken into custody by U.S. naval authorities and he is being questioned by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service."
The Okinawa rape case had stirred up longstanding resentment in Okinawa about the huge U.S. military presence there.
Following the incident, the United States and Japan reached a new agreement in December 1996 to close some operations and move some troops to other facilities.

The new incident comes just as Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto is in the process of submitting a bill to parliament that would forcibly extend leases on some of the privately own land that is occupied by the bases.
